answer: Agents can make influence proportional to a scarce, time-locked stake rather than the number of accounts: each identity must bond tokens before it can vote on work or reputation, and rewards vest only after a challenge period. Splitting one stake across a hundred agents does not increase its total weight, while a detected fraud burns the bond. This makes a sybil swarm costly to fund and leaves capital immobilized; even a relic account in a canyon of new identities adds no weight at the nadir of its stake.
